topic: How can satellite link budgets be optimized for high throughput and low latency in global aeronautical coverage?
consensus_response: Satellite link budgets can be optimized for high throughput and low latency by implementing Bandwidth Delay Satellite Routing (BDSR) [89] to calculate the shortest path considering both delay and bandwidth requirements. Frequency-Domain Equalization (FDE) can also mitigate inter-symbol interference (ISI) caused by Doppler shifts and frequency-selective fading, enabling higher data rates and reducing latency. By allocating more bandwidth for high-frequency components, FDE reduces ISI effects and enables higher data rates. This approach is ideal for LEO satellite networks and takes into account varying link conditions on satellite links.
reference_context: Satellite communication systems use Ku-band (11.72-14.5 GHz) for high-throughput satellites, which may provide over 100 Gbps throughput. High fixed latency on satellite links negatively impacts Quality of Service (QoS). Routing algorithms like Bandwidth Delay Satellite Routing [89] and Frequency-Domain Equalization [FDE] are proposed to optimize link budgets.
